gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the loudness gap in dB across all four amps it showed. From the maker-rated 8 Ω power, the $2,000 Marantz Model 50 (70 W) plays only 0.67 dB louder than the 60 W Yamaha A-S301 or WiiM Amp Pro. The 45 W Denon PMA-600NE gives up 1.25 dB to the 60 W pair and 1.92 dB to the Marantz.
standout_why: I read hifiaudiosource.com (Yamaha A-S301 vs Denon PMA-600NE), recordplayeradvice.com (Denon vs Yamaha) and stylusandsound.com (integrated amps under $1,000). The What Hi-Fi best-buys page returned only its title. Hifiaudiosource already puts the Yamaha-vs-Denon gap at 'a bit over 1 dB' (and 'a decibel or two' in its FAQ) and gives both list prices, but it doesn't calculate cost per watt. Stylusandsound states the general rule '3 dB more sensitive needs half the amplifier power' but applies it to no amp. No rival gives the dB gap for the Marantz Model 50 or the WiiM Amp Pro, the 4 Ω gap between the WiiM and the Denon, or cost per watt. Our page would add the four-amp version and dollars per watt, not a new kind of fact.
decides: Confirms that wattage shouldn't decide between these picks. A 0.67 to 1.92 dB spread is about the smallest change in level most people can notice. So the extra $1,570 for the Marantz over the Yamaha ($2,000 vs $429.95) buys under 1 dB at 8 Ω. That spend has to be justified by build or sound, not loudness. On rated 8 Ω power the Yamaha costs about half as much per watt as the Denon ($7.17 vs $13.31). The Denon is the only one of the four rated at 45 W, but that matters only with low-sensitivity speakers in a large room.
